title: Embodied fly, stage 3b: a perturbation test of the claw-neuron resistance reflex: does feedback that follows an imposed flexion bring the grooming leg back faster? (SIMULATED, closed loop)
status: registered before any perturbed closed-loop simulation
relation_to_parent: Stage 3a's go/no-go failed (resistance feedback moved the held tibia by 0.0054 rad) and stays failed. It showed why a held posture cannot test a reflex: the claw neurons fire at a near-constant rate, so contingent and blind input coincide (the sham matched the resistance arm at the motor level). The classic test perturbs the joint. Stage 3b imposes a brief flexion during the held reach and measures the return. Its sham keeps the tonic feedback but removes the part that follows the perturbation: each sham trial receives the claw rates of the same seed's unperturbed resistance trial.
seen_before_registration: every stage-3a result (seeds 1020-1027): under grooming drive the tibia holds at a median 0.6337 rad open loop; resistance feedback lowers tibia extensor rates from 43.25 to 31.75 Hz and raises flexor rates from 0.1 to 3.4 Hz; the sham gives 33.25 and 3.0 Hz; claw rates about 90 Hz during the hold; exploratory, at r_full 80 Hz the tibia moves from 0.6546 to 0.6705 rad under resistance and to 0.6711 under the sham

body only (no neural input), extensor held at full activation: the tibia rests at 0.634 rad; a 20 ms torque on the femur-tibia joint of 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 (model units, flexing) gives a peak excursion of 0.030, 0.058, 0.107, 0.243, 0.625, 3.565 rad and a return to within 0.05 rad of the pre-pulse angle 0, 0, 3, 9, 27, 142 ms after the pulse

design.everything_else: exactly stage 3a: the stage-1c male nerve cord (LIF, w_syn 0.275 mV), grooming drive (DNg62 + DNge078, 150 Hz) and no drive, the FlyMimic leg and muscle map, the 1 ms loop, the four left front-leg claw neurons, their linear tuning and suprathreshold Poisson delivery, the resistance and assistance assignments
design.perturbation: a torque of 10 (model units) flexing the femur-tibia joint, held from 0.500 to 0.520 s of the 1 s trial

arms.resistance_unperturbed: the resistance arm without the perturbation (used to build the sham; reported)
arms.sham: perturbed; each claw neuron receives the rate time course it had in the same seed's resistance_unperturbed trial

design.trials: 16 per arm under grooming drive, seeds 1030-1045; the open, resistance and assistance arms also without drive
design.r_full: 20 Hz (as every stage); the open, resistance and sham arms repeated at 80 Hz as sensitivity, reported without prediction
design.readouts: pre-pulse angle: median femur-tibia angle 0.40-0.50 s; excursion: maximum angle 0.50-0.60 s minus the pre-pulse angle; recovery time: ms after the pulse ends (0.520 s) until the angle first comes within 0.05 rad of the pre-pulse angle (the trial's remaining time if never); also time near the head, pool rates and claw rates

M0_the_push_moves_the_leg.statement: Precondition: the perturbation flexes the held tibia
M0_the_push_moves_the_leg.test: open-loop median excursion under grooming >= 0.2 rad; if not, M1-M3 are uninterpretable

M1_feedback_speeds_the_return.statement: The resistance assignment brings the tibia back faster than the open loop
M1_feedback_speeds_the_return.test: median recovery time in the resistance arm <= 0.8 x the open-loop median (grooming)

M2_the_speed_needs_the_loop.statement: The faster return comes from feedback that follows the perturbation, not from the tonic input
M2_the_speed_needs_the_loop.test: interpretable only if M1 passes: median recovery time in the resistance arm < the sham median

M3_the_opposite_assignment_does_not_spee.statement: The direction comes from which claw type carries which tuning
M3_the_opposite_assignment_does_not_spee.test: median recovery time in the assistance arm >= the open-loop median

M4_the_reach_survives.statement: The perturbed, closed-loop leg still grooms
M4_the_reach_survives.test: median time near the head in the resistance arm under grooming >= 0.5 and at least 0.25 above the no-drive median

not_claimed_even_if_all_pass: that the fly's resistance reflex runs through these neurons or is tuned this way: the tuning assignment is a stated bracket, tuning is linear, one leg and one proprioceptor class; a pass means the male-CNS wiring of the front-leg claw neurons, closed through a muscle-driven leg, returns an imposed flexion faster when SNpp51 carry extension, because of feedback that follows the perturbation
reporting: Every prediction with its value and pass/fail or uninterpretable, whichever way it falls; excursions, recovery times, pool and claw rates per arm; the r_full 80 Hz sensitivity.
